title: Shrinkflation Receipt
sendTrigger: Send this to whoever does the groceries.
editorialNotes: Shrinkflation weight-change figures (16oz->13.5oz, Oreo family-size change) are documented consumer-reporting cases from 2023-2025, not a single hero-eligible citation - kept as evidence-log items, never hero type.

8-12% figure is the carousel's own aggregate framing of the documented cases above, not sourced to a single study - rendered as the slide 4 hero because the brief explicitly stages it that way, consistent with the receipt thread's own running total.

thread.element: receipt tape, prints one line per slide
thread.endState: full receipt, total stamped "+8-12% - charged, not shown."

copy.headline: The price didn't go up. The box got smaller.
copy.body: Two products, same shelf, same price. One of them is quietly lying to you.

copy.headline: It's shrinkflation.
items: Less product inside. The packaging barely changes, so you don't notice.

copy.headline: The evidence log
items: A "family size" package of cookies is now the size a regular package used to be.

copy.heroNumberCaption: The effective price increase on a bag of chips isn't 0%. They just hid it in the packaging instead of the price tag.

copy.headline: What you check versus what you don't
copy.body: Companies count on this: people notice price increases but not size decreases.

copy.heroNumberCaption: Cost per ounce is the number the store doesn't want you looking at. It's printed on the shelf tag, smaller than the price.
copy.body: Check that number, not the sticker price.

copy.headline: The price didn't change. Your serving count did.
copy.ctaLine: fond tracks what you actually get per dollar, not what the box says.
